subject.title: [Reliability]: Enforce atomic intent→execution flow to prevent orphan pre-action notices

question: Should OpenClaw add a public transaction lifecycle contract for agent runs now, and should that contract be separate from or folded into the structured process-events work?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the fix defines new public lifecycle semantics across protocol, runtime, sessions, clients, and possibly policy/config, so automation cannot safely choose the durable contract shape.

options.title: Design Additive Transaction Contract
options.body: Define run.begin, execution evidence, run.commit/run.abort, structured blocker payloads, compatibility behavior, and tests as a core protocol/runtime contract.

options.title: Fold Into Process Events
options.body: Use the open structured process-events work as the source of truth and make this issue's commit/abort guarantees acceptance criteria there.

options.title: Keep Strict-Agentic Only
options.body: Treat shipped strict-agentic handling as sufficient for false-starts and close or narrow this issue to docs and telemetry only.

recommendation.title: Design Additive Transaction Contract
recommendation.body: Define run.begin, execution evidence, run.commit/run.abort, structured blocker payloads, compatibility behavior, and tests as a core protocol/runtime contract.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already provided the prior keep-open product-contract review and has recent adjacent terminal-outcome history.
